sentences.text: ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

In this appeal, challenge is to the judgment and award dated 30.10.2013 passed by learned Joint Civil Judge, Senior Division, Nagpur (for short "Reference Court") in L.A.C. No.13/1999, whereby the reference application made by the appellants came to be dismissed.

2. Background facts :
The appellants are the owners of house bearing No. 182 and 208, situated at Mouza - Kachari Sawanga, Tah. Katol, Dist. Nagpur.
The house property with the plots was acquired for Kanholi Nala project by the respondents.
Notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was issued on 29.08.1992 .
The award was passed on 31.03.1995.
The SLAO awarded compensation of Rs.1,17,313/- for the structure as well as for the open plot.
The compensation was accepted under protest.
It is the grievance of the appellants that the market price of the construction and open plot was 3 FA951.16 (J).odt not properly determined.
The compensation awarded was meagre.
At the relevant time, the market price of the open land was Rs.20/- per sq.ft. and the valuation of the constructed area was more than Rs.35/- per sq.mtr.
The appellant, therefore, claimed for enhancement of the compensation.
3. The respondents filed their written statement and opposed the reference.
According to the respondents, the compensation awarded by the SLAO was just, proper and reasonable.
All the factors relevant for the purpose of determining the market price had been taken into consideration.
Learned Reference Court framed the issues.
Evidence on affidavit of appellant no.1 - Wasudeo Tukaram Bolke was filed.
Learned Reference Court, on consideration of the evidence found that the compensation awarded was just, proper and reasonable and accordingly dismissed the reference.
Being aggrieved by this judgment and order, the appellants have come before this Court in appeal.
4. I have heard Mrs. S.K. Paunikar, learned advocate for the appellants and Mr. M.A. Kadu, learned Assistant Government Pleader for the respondents.
Perused the record and proceedings.

Following points fall for my determination :
i] Whether the compensation awarded in respect of the constructed area is just,
proper and reasonable ? ii]

Whether the compensation in respect of the open plot of land awarded by the SLAO is just, proper and reasonable ? iii] What Order ?
6.
Learned advocate Mrs. Paunikar for the appellants submitted that learned Reference Court has not taken into consideration the evidence adduced by the appellants.
Learned advocate pointed out that the Valuer could not be examined inasmuch as at the relevant time, the Valuer was not available.
Learned advocate for the appellants in this appeal has made a separate application seeking permission to lead additional evidence and grant leave to examine the Valuer.

Learned advocate submitted that the Reference Court has not taken into consideration the decisions in the land reference cases of the same village in respect of the similarly situated construction and open plot of land.
Learned advocate submitted that therefore, the judgment and order passed by the Reference Court is not sustainable.
7. Learned Assistant Government Pleader Mr. Kadu submitted that there is hardly any evidence on record to prove the 5 FA951.16 (J).odt nature of construction.
Learned AGP submitted that the market price of the constructed area has to be determined taking into consideration the nature of construction and the material used for the construction.
Learned AGP submitted that in the affidavit of evidence of the witness examined by the appellants, the witness is conspicuously silent about all these facts.
Learned AGP submitted that the Reference Court was right in rejecting the claim for enhancement with regard to the construction as well as plot.
As far as the application for leading additional evidence is concerned, learned AGP submitted that ample opportunity was granted to the appellants to examine the Valuer.
Learned AGP submitted that the reasons stated in the application are not cogent and convincing to accept the contention.
In short, learned AGP prayed for dismissal of the appeal as well as application for leading additional evidence.

8. At the outset, it would be necessary to consider the application bearing Civil Application (CAF)
No. 3135/2023 made for leading additional evidence.
It is to be noted that this appeal was filed in the year 2016.
This appeal was heard by me partly on three dates.
Immediately on filing of the appeal, the appellant did not make 6 FA951.16 (J).odt application for leading additional evidence.
Perusal of the record of the Reference Court would show that the Reference Court had granted sufficient opportunity to the appellant to lead oral and documentary evidence.
It is also not the grievance of the appellants that the Reference Court had denied the opportunity to examine the Valuer.
It is stated that at the relevant time, the Valuer was not available and therefore, he could not be examined.
It is stated that due to his personal reason, he had refused to come to the Court.
It is pertinent to note that in such an important matter, the Advocate, by making appropriate application before the Reference Court, could have secured presence of the Valuer.
The report of the Valuer, in the absence of his oral evidence, was not exhibited.

sentences.text:
The question is whether at this stage, an opportunity to lead additional evidence, as stated above,
can be granted or not.
In order to allow a party to lead additional evidence, it must be established that after exercising due diligence, the party concerned could not examine the witness/produce evidence.
Unless and until it is established that despite exercising due diligence, the evidence was neither known or could not be adduced, such indulgence cannot be 7 FA951.16 (J).odt granted in the appeal.
Even an application was not made before the Reference Court for the purpose of securing presence of the Valuer.
It is to be noted that at the last moment of these appeals, the application has been moved.
In my opinion, the appellants have not made out a case to allow them to lead additional evidence.
Therefore, this application deserves to be rejected.

10. Learned advocate for the appellants took me through the judgment and order passed by the Reference Court and pointed out that the Reference Court has made a reference to the earlier decisions of the Reference Court in L.A.C. Nos. 124/1999, 284/1995, 411/2002 and 91/1997.
Learned advocate submitted that in these Reference cases, the house and open plots involved were from same village.

Learned advocate, therefore, submitted that by invoking the principle of parity,
the compensation awarded in these Reference cases ought to have been given in respect of the property of the appellants.
11. It is to be noted that as far as construction is concerned, there cannot be any straight jacket formula for the purpose of quantifying the market price.
It depends on number of factors.

Some 8 FA951.16 (J).odt of the factors could be the location of the house, nature of construction of the house, year of construction of the house and the material used for construction of the house etc.
All these facts must be proved by leading cogent evidence.
In this case, the report of the Valuer has not been exhibited.
The report, therefore, cannot be read in evidence.
The only evidence that is available on record is the affidavit of examination- in- chief of witness no.1.
It is true that in absence of the advocate for the respondents, cross-examination of this witness could not be conducted.
Be that as it may, the question remains as to whether this evidence is sufficient to prove the above factors.
Bare perusal of the examination-in-chief of witness no.1 would show that it is conspicuously silent about all the above stated factors.
Learned Reference Court has, therefore, recorded a finding that as far as the above stated factors are concerned, there is no evidence at all.
On going through the record, it is seen that there is no evidence as far as above referred factors are concerned.

In my view, therefore,
as far as the constructed area is concerned, no case is made out to warrant interference in the judgment and order passed by the Reference Court.
12. The next important aspect is with regard to the market 9 FA951.16 (J).odt price of the open plot awarded by the SLAO.
Learned advocate for the appellants submitted that in respect of the acquired open plots from the same village, the compensation awarded was @ Rs.15/- per sq. ft.
Learned advocate submitted that the Reference Court has considered this fact, but failed to award the same.

It is seen on perusal of the judgment of the Reference Court that the Reference Court has referred to the decisions in the above stated land reference cases, wherein the compensation in respect of the open plots was granted @ Rs.15/- per sq.ft.
In my view, therefore, the Reference Court was required to invoke the principle of parity and should have determined the compensation of the open plots accordingly.
As far as open plots are concerned, there would not have been much difference.
The property is situated in the same village.

Learned Reference Court, therefore, was required to take Wasudeo Bolke (Dead) Thr Lrs Ashish ... vs State Of Maharashtra Through ... on 10 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112390316/
4 this fact into consideration.

sentences.text: It is seen that in respect of the open land, the market price determined by the SLAO was Rs.3.25/- per sq.ft.
The Reference Court has failed to take this fact into consideration.
In my view, therefore, the Reference Court in this case ought to have awarded the compensation @ Rs.15/- per sq.ft. in respect of the open plot/area.
As far as the finding on this point is concerned, I am of the view that it cannot be sustained.
The appellants, in my view, 10 FA951.16 (J).odt would be entitled to get compensation in respect of the open area of the land @ Rs.15/- per sq.ft. with interest and other consequential benefits.
Accordingly, I record my finding on point no.1 in negative and on point no.2 in affirmative.
As a result of this, the appeal deserves to be partly allowed.
13. Accordingly, the First Appeal is partly allowed.

(i) The judgment and award dated 30.10.2013 passed by learned Joint Civil Judge,
Senior Division, Nagpur in L.A.C. No. 13/1999 is set aside to the extent of open land/plot.
(ii) The claim to the extent of open land is allowed.
The appellants are held entitled to get compensation in respect of open land @ Rs.15/- per sq.ft.
(iii) The appellants are entitled to get interest and other statutory benefits on this enhanced amount of compensation.
(iv) The amount of compensation paid in respect of the open plot of land in terms of the award passed by the SLAO be adjusted.
Decree be drawn up accordingly.
( G. A. SANAP, J. ) Diwale Signed by: DIWALE
